daily_quests.title: ASX 200 Stock Momentum Ranking with Window Functions
daily_quests.description: Using ASX 200 historical price data, calculate the 30-day price momentum for each stock using window functions. For each stock, compute: (1) ROW_NUMBER() to rank stocks by closing price within each date window, (2) LAG() to fetch the closing price from 30 days ago, (3) momentum as percentage change, (4) RANK() to rank stocks by momentum descending within each date. Filter to show only the top 10 momentum gainers and top 10 momentum losers for the most recent date in the dataset. Expected output: stock_code, current_price, price_30_days_ago, momentum_percent, momentum_rank, date.

daily_quests.title: NSW Road Crash Data Cleaning and Injury Classification
daily_quests.description: Download NSW Road Crash Data (data.nsw.gov.au). Clean the dataset by: (1) handling missing values in injury_level and crash_type columns (document your strategy), (2) standardising datetime formats in the crash_date column, (3) removing duplicate records based on crash_id, (4) creating a new column severity_category that classifies crashes as 'Fatal', 'Serious', 'Minor', or 'Non-Injury' based on injury_level values, (5) exporting the cleaned dataset to CSV. Produce a summary report showing: record count before/after cleaning, percentage of missing values by column, and distribution of crashes by severity_category.

daily_quests.title: Melbourne Pedestrian Traffic Analysis Pipeline
daily_quests.description: Build an end-to-end pipeline: (1) In Python/pandas, download Melbourne pedestrian counting data (Melbourne Open Data Portal), clean it by removing null counts and standardising sensor location names, then aggregate hourly pedestrian counts by location and hour-of-day. (2) Load the cleaned data into a SQL database (SQLite or PostgreSQL). (3) In SQL, write a query using CTEs and window functions to: identify the peak hour (hour_of_day with highest total pedestrians) for each sensor location, calculate the percentage contribution of each location to total daily foot traffic, and rank locations by average hourly pedestrian count. (4) Export results showing: location, peak_hour, avg_pedestrians, total_daily_pedestrians, pct_contribution_to_total, location_rank. Expected output: CSV with ranked analysis of top 15 locations by traffic volume.
